rec.name: Hero Banner with Social Proof Pill, Headline, CTA and Product Mockup

what.text: A dark, full-width hero banner for the top of the homepage. Order of content: a small social-proof line (final copy: "€5,000,000 additional revenue from A/B-tested Sectionfy sections"), a large headline ("Shopify sections that sell"), a short sub-headline ("Our sections are based on real A/B test results and integrate into any Shopify theme in seconds"), and one bright green CTA button ("Discover all possibilities"). On the right (desktop) or below the text (mobile) sits a tilted phone mockup with floating UI cards that show the product's sections in use, for example a free-gift progress bar and a customer-count social-proof chip. A separate mobile image is used, with soft fades at the top and bottom edges so it blends into the page.

why.text: The social-proof line puts a hard, quantified result in front of the visitor before they read anything else, which builds credibility. The headline and sub-headline state the benefit (sections that sell, based on real A/B tests) and remove friction (fast integration). The product mockup shows the offer instead of describing it. A single high-contrast CTA gives a clear next step. The mobile fade avoids a hard visual break, so the page feels continuous and the content is easier to scan.

how.text: Design the hero as two images: a desktop banner (2800x1000 px) and a mobile banner (1200x1600 px). Upload them to the theme's image banner section, using the 'Image' and 'Mobile image' slots. Create the mockup (phone plus floating cards) in a design tool or 3D tool, and export a version with text and a version without. Preferred approach: keep the text (social-proof line, headline, sub-headline, CTA) as live Shopify text rather than baked into the image, so screen readers can read it and the copy is easy to edit. Export the images at full quality, because early uploads looked blurry. On mobile, add a gradient fade at the top and bottom of the image instead of a hard edge. Placing the heading on top of the image with no gap would need custom code, so the fade was chosen instead.

items: Text baked into the image vs. live Shopify text (live text recommended for accessibility)
Mobile edge fade (top and bottom) built into the mobile image

dependencies.text: Needs a theme banner section with separate desktop and mobile image pickers, which the Sectionfy theme already has. No app is needed. Text overlaid on the image, or a heading placed directly on the image with no gap, would need custom Liquid/CSS. The mockup artwork must be produced separately (design or 3D tool).

items: Conversion rate from homepage visit to purchase (or sign-up)
LCP / image load time (large hero images)
